summary: Recovered J100 and J101 exactly once into the persistent CUPS queue `archive`. Their archived payloads are byte-identical, original spool files remain, new raw jobs archive correctly, and the configuration survived a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine-compatible CUPS 2.4.18 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created an atomic, retry-idempotent electronic archive backend writing one file per CUPS job under /srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed.
Enabled CUPS through OpenRC and created the enabled, accepting raw queue `archive`.
Submitted J100 and J101 once each and verified their archived bytes.
Tested new raw submissions before and after reboot.
Restarted node1 once and verified changed boot identity plus full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Recover every job in spool/jobs.tsv exactly once
evidence.summary: Single submissions produced archive-1 and archive-2; output count advanced from zero to one to two.

evidence.requirement: Retain payload bytes and original spool files
evidence.summary: J100 and J101 sources remain present, and each source/output pair has matching SHA-256 hashes and successful byte comparisons before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Provide a working persistent CUPS queue named archive
evidence.summary: The archive queue is enabled, accepting, idle, defaulted to archive-store:/, and cupsd/dbus are enabled at boot.

evidence.requirement: Route new raw jobs to the printed directory
evidence.summary: New raw jobs archive-3 and archive-4 created one file each with exact expected hashes, including a successful post-restart submission.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 70e1cc37-eabf-4eb3-96a2-6e66cfebaae0, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 28707dad-a28d-442a-bae5-06602dc51649, recovered service/data, and successful post-restart printing are directly proven.
